newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Oct 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Oct 16.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- DELAY IN SEALING DEALS THREATENS CREST TIMETABLE

Difficulties in the reconciliation of trades could threaten the timetable for paperless trading according to Crestco, the company running the City's automated share settlement system. Crestco blame companies registrars for the delays but said they are working closely with them to make sure the problems do not occur. So far only 223 stocks can be traded through Crest which was introduced in July, but the City is aiming for a complete switch from the paper based Talisman system by next April.
-- CITY WINS MORE BOND BUSINESS

A further indication of London's strength as a financial centre compared with Frankfurt was delivered yesterday as Dresdner Kleinwort Benson announced that it is to bring its eurobond business to London. The move accompanies an announcement that the bank is to buy Luthy, Baillie, Dowsett, Pethick & Co, one of the City's most prestigious bond broking boutiques.
THE TIMES
-- STERLING RISE GAINS FRESH MOMENTUM

The rise of sterling gathered a new momentum yesterday, the pound leaping by more than two pfennigs to 2.4380 marks from Monday's 2.4170 marks to reach its highest level for almost two years. In US trading it broke the 2.44 marks level and in its trade-weighted index against a basket of currencies, it closed at 88.6, from 88.0 on Monday.
-- BARCLAYS SETS UP NEW FUND BUSINESS TO INVEST 239 BILLION STG

Barclays set up a new fund business yesterday and created the worlds second largest. Second only to Fidelity of the US, the fund management business will look after 230 billion stg belonging to pension funds, charities and insurance companies. Barclays Global Investors was born from the merger of BZW Barclays Global Investors and BZW Investment Management and also incorporates last year's $440 million acquisition of Wells Fargo Nikko Investment Advisers.
-- UNITED NEWS WINS BATTLE OF BLENHEIM

United News & Media finally won the long auction of Blenheim Group, gaining control of the exhibitions business with a 592.5 million stg cash offer. Blenheim's chairman, Neville Buch, will get more than 27 million stg for his shareholding. Blenheim are supporting the 500p a share offer, allowing United to secure 51 per cent of the company.
THE GUARDIAN
-- BREWER IS BIG CHEESE AFTER BIDDING 90 MILLION STG

Whitbread look set to take over Brightreasons, the Pizzaland restaurant chain owner. The offer from the brewing firm is believed to be around 90 million stg for the 180-branch group. Whitbread is thought to have outbid City Centre Restaurants, the owners of the Deep Pan Pizza and Garfunkels chains.
-- WATER COMPANIES' PRICE PROSPECTS DOUBLY DAMMED

A double blow was dealt to water companies yesterday with news that Ofwat, the industry regulator, intends to put an end to continually increasing bills and that the Government may extend its powers. Ian Byatt, the director-general of Ofwat, said that he planned to re-examine the industry's price controls in 1999, which is five years sooner than he has to. As well as this, a leaked Department of the Environment report on water resources said the Government was considering requests by Ofwat and the Environment Agency for refinements or extensions of their powers.
-- PEUGEOT'S NEW 'BABY' TO BE BORN AT RYTON

Peugeot, the French car company, is to make a second car at its Ryton plant near Coventry. Hundreds of millions will be invested in a new "baby" 206 which will secure the factory's future and its 2.600 jobs. The investment, which is due to be announced formally in the new year, will also create hundreds of more jobs among component suppliers.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- PROPERTY WIZARD SEEKS BACKERS FOR A RUSSIAN FLUTTER

ALEA, the Bermuda registered company with backing from property industry luminary Elliot Bernerd, is planning to set up an on-line lottery in 10 Russian cities. Alea will be the way for UK investors to get into the Russian national lottery, a joint venture between Alea with 60 per cent and its Russian partner, the Russian Committee for the Protection of Peace, with 40 per cent. The company has plans for lotteries around the emerging world.
-- GRIM FORECAST ON DIRECT LINE PROFITS HITS RBS SHARES

Shares in the Royal Bank of Scotland were hit yesterday as BZW's top-rated analyst Hugh Pye cut his forecasts for the company's Direct Line insurance subsidiary because of sustained pricing pressure on premiums as well as a big increase in liability claims. BZW recommended its clients to sell RBS shares, after cutting its forecast for Direct Line's profits from 50 to 16 million stg for 1995/96. The shares in RBS dropped 13p to 522.5.
-- GEHE SELLS DRUG MANUFACTURING OPERATIONS

Gehe, the German drugs group, announced yesterday its plans to sell its last drug manufacturing operations in a bid to concentrate on expanding further in drugs wholesaling. Gehe stated that the move was not related to its two-way battle with UniChem for Lloyds Chemists. The company said that it believed its manufacturing operations were not large enough to compete in the consolidating pharmaceuticals market and it expects to gain near to 500 million stg from the sale of the four manufacturing divisions.
